review.notes: Triage review: full structural/fence scan (all fences balanced, no swallowed headings/tables/images); automated whole-document page-text diff (normalized 4-gram containment per page) with manual inspection of every page below 0.90 coverage, plus decimal-number completeness checks on all table-heavy pages (1, 4, 8, 11-16, 18-19, 43-46, 63, 65-66, 74-81, 83: zero missing values). Rendered and visually inspected: page 1 footnote area, page 50 (300 dpi word-level crop), page 83 (rubric posters), plus section-structure cross-checks over pages 45-93. Appendix B example conversations exist only as embedded figure screenshots in the print itself and are not transcription defects. Line-by-line reading was limited to the flagged low-coverage pages, the title page, and appendix D.8; the remaining pages were machine-scanned only.

unresolved.evidence: Appendix D.8.1/D.8.2/D.8.3 print five-column rubric posters (Relevant/Valid/Inclusive/Reliable/Actionable with 0 limited/1 okay/2 good/3 great chips). The OCR interleaves the columns, promotes poster titles, column labels and score-chip texts to headings (## Rubric for RAI Measurement Quality For each dimension..., ## Relevant..., ## 2 good, ## 1 okay, ## 3 great), drops the "0 limited" chip text, and omits cells in D.8.3 (e.g. "May overestimate performance if translation system is not sufficiently capable (eg, early training)." printed on p.84). A page-by-page reconstruction of the three posters is needed before restructuring.

Pages with 4-gram coverage below 0.90 that are conversation/figure-example pages (Persian proverbs Figures 1-2, translation demos, creative-generation figures, coding demos) were only machine-scanned; their text exists inside embedded figure screenshots in both print conventions and the OCR embeds the figures, but line-level confirmation of every caption and embed pairing was not completed within budget.
